title.en: Viability-preserving transformative continuation order separating evolution from widening and churn

statement.en: TransformativeViable and TransformsViably preserve substrate viability and macro capability option-space across micro-turnover while retiring legacy forms, strictly separating constructive evolution from zero-loss Widens and destructive churn on finite balanced gainless worlds.

laws.en: Transformative viability order: MacroAdmits reads capability existence via W.Admits (l t) t f; widens_implies_transformativeViable shows Web.Widens ⊆ TransformativeViable under ReserveGuarded W Viable and Viable l'; TransformsViably requires permanent ViableT, non-shrinking MacroAdmits, and step-by-step micro-turnover (ruling out trivial stasis), connected to Web.Linked via TransformsViablyAlong and transformsViably_iff_along_capSame.

Three-regime separation: on ThreeRegime.web with non-constant Cap, l_evolve retires legacy fOld while enabling fNew and fPlus (Mixed l_evolve l_legacy, ¬ Widens, yet StrictTransformativeViable), whereas l_churn exhibits «全生成» next «一» (Steps.same QChurn) 1 yet fails both Viable and MacroIncludes.

Finite balanced gainless escape: FiniteGainless constructs a three-condition closed, balanced, Conserving (hence Flow.Gainless) web with RequiresWithin all where Flow.whole_not_keepsWidening forbids KeepsWidening Web.itself web.level 0 while TransformsViably (fun t => 1 ≤ web.level t .cSub) cap 0 holds perpetually alongside explicit micro_turnover.

hypotheses.en: No axiom. Uses Web.Admits (l t) t f; widens_implies_transformativeViable assumes ReserveGuarded W Viable and Viable l'; TransformsViably requires non-trivial cap : F → K, ViableT, non-shrinking MacroAdmits, and step-by-step micro-turnover.

does_not_show.en: Any canonical choice of capability projection cap : F → K or substrate Viable predicate for empirical socio-technical systems.
Extension to non-finite or open external-renewal growth regimes beyond finite ClosedAt webs.
